question: India's double fortification of salt (DFS) adds which two micronutrients to address the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies simultaneously?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Double Fortified Salt (DFS) combines iodine (to prevent iodine deficiency disorders/goitre) and iron (to prevent iron-deficiency anaemia). India uses DFS in many government nutrition programmes including the ICDS and mid-day meal scheme.
Vitamin A is not added to salt. Vitamin A fortification in India is applied to vegetable oils and vanaspati, not salt. DFS adds iodine and iron.
Iron and folic acid are combined in IFA tablets (supplementation), not in salt fortification. DFS adds iodine and iron, not folic acid.
Zinc is not a component of the current Indian DFS programme. The two micronutrients in double fortified salt are iodine and iron.

overallFeedback.feedback: Double Fortified Salt (DFS) adds iodine (preventing goitre/IDD) and iron (preventing iron-deficiency anaemia) — the two most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies in India.
Well done! Double Fortified Salt (iodine + iron) is a key mass fortification strategy addressing both IDD and iron-deficiency anaemia simultaneously.
